issues.display_title: Issue #475: Migrate API Queries to GORM Models Category
issues.main_description_html:
RESULT 03/08/26

✅ Implementation: GORM Model Query Migration Category

Overview

This document outlines the first implementation step for migrating API queries from raw Table(...) usage to GORM Model(...) usage.

Initial target:

  • GET /categories
  • File: src/Action/V1/Categories/ListCategories.go

Files Modified

  1. src/Action/V1/Categories/ListCategories.go

Implementation Details

1. Query Target Update

Replaced raw table targeting:

Config.DB.Table("categories").Select("id, name")

with GORM model targeting:

Config.DB.Model(&Models.Categories{}).
    Select("id, name").
    Order("id ASC").
    Scan(&categoriesData)

2. Response Preservation

The API still scans into:

[]Models.CategoriesData

This keeps the response payload unchanged:

{
  "id": 1,
  "name": "Example"
}

The table model Models.Categories includes fields like created_at and updated_at, so the response DTO is kept to avoid exposing extra fields.

3. No Manual Mapping Loop

The query uses GORM Scan(&categoriesData) directly.

This avoids unnecessary manual mapping loops while still binding the query to the table model.

Verification

Ran:

go test ./...

Result: pass.

Objective

Migrate API queries from raw table targeting with Config.DB.Table(...) to GORM model targeting with Config.DB.Model(&Models.X{}), one API at a time, without changing existing API response shape.

Requirements

1. Work Per API

  • Update one API endpoint at a time.
  • Start from small, low-risk APIs.
  • Verify each API before moving to the next one.

Initial API:

  • GET /categories via src/Action/V1/Categories/ListCategories.go

2. Use GORM Table Models

Replace query patterns like:

Config.DB.Table("categories").Select("id, name")

with:

Config.DB.Model(&Models.Categories{}).Select("id, name")

Use the table/view models added under src/Models.

3. Preserve Response Models When Needed

  • Do not force table models into responses if they would add/remove/change JSON fields.
  • If the response DTO already matches the API contract, keep scanning into that DTO.
  • Avoid manual mapping loops when GORM can scan selected columns directly into the response DTO.

Preferred pattern:

var categoriesData []Models.CategoriesData

Config.DB.Model(&Models.Categories{}).
    Select("id, name").
    Order("id ASC").
    Scan(&categoriesData)

This keeps the query bound to the table model while preserving the old response shape.

4. Do Not Change API Responses

  • Do not expose table-only fields such as created_at or updated_at unless the API already returned them.
  • Do not rename JSON keys.
  • Do not change cache payload shape.
  • Do not change pagination, ordering, encryption, or response wrapper behavior.

5. Verification

Run after each API update:

go test ./...

If an endpoint has API collection examples or manual test data, compare the response shape before and after the change.

First Implementation Target

src/Action/V1/Categories/ListCategories.go

Expected update:

  • Use Config.DB.Model(&Models.Categories{}).
  • Keep scanning into []Models.CategoriesData.
  • Keep cached JSON and response payload unchanged.
  • Avoid manual mapping loops.

issues.display_title: Issue #476: Hashtag GORM Model Query Migration
issues.main_description_html:
RESULT 03/08/26

✅ Implementation: Hashtag GORM Model Query Migration

Overview

This document outlines the Hashtag module query migration for non-slim APIs.

The implementation changes Hashtag APIs from raw Table(...) usage to GORM Model(...) usage with table/view models, while keeping response DTOs where needed so the API response shape does not change.

APIs Updated

  1. GET /search/hashtag
  2. GET /search/hashtag-post

Slim routes were intentionally skipped:

  1. GET /search/sl/hashtag
  2. GET /search/sl/post-by-hashtag

Files Added

  1. src/Models/ViewsHashtag.go
  2. src/Models/HashtagByUser.go
  3. src/Models/ViewsTimelinePostSlim.go

Files Modified

  1. src/Action/V1/Hashtag/SearchHashtag.go
  2. src/Action/V1/Hashtag/SearchHashtagPost.go
  3. src/Models/ViewsHashtag.go

Implementation Details

1. views_hashtag Model

Added Models.ViewsHashtag for the views_hashtag view.

Internal filter fields are hidden from JSON:

Encrypt    string `gorm:"column:encrypt" json:"-"`
CategoryID int    `gorm:"column:category_id" json:"-"`

This keeps the fields available for GORM filters while preventing accidental response exposure.

2. hashtag_by_user Model

Added Models.HashtagByUser for the hashtag_by_user view.

It supports queries that select:

tag, count as total_posts, counter

and scan into the existing response DTO.

3. views_timeline_post_slim Model

Added Models.ViewsTimelinePostSlim for the views_timeline_post_slim view.

The API still scans selected columns into Models.HashtagPost to preserve the existing response payload.

4. SearchHashtag.go

Updated query targets:

Config.DB.Model(&Models.ViewsHashtag{})
Config.DB.Model(&Models.HashtagByUser{})

Changed intermediate query result from []Models.HashtagData to []Models.ViewsHashtag where the data source is views_hashtag.

5. SearchHashtagPost.go

Updated query targets:

Config.DB.Model(&Models.ViewsHashtag{})
Config.DB.Model(&Models.ViewsTimelinePostSlim{})

Replaced:

[]map[string]interface{}

with:

[]Models.ViewsHashtag

The API still extracts slugs for the second query and scans final post data into []Models.HashtagPost so the response remains unchanged.

Hashtag Parameter Note

If the response shows:

"hashtag": ""

check whether the request used an unencoded #.

Correct request:

/search/hashtag-post?tag=%23happy

Incorrect request:

/search/hashtag-post?tag=#happy

The unencoded # becomes a URL fragment and does not reach the server.

Verification

Ran:

go test ./...

Result: pass.

Objective

Update non-slim Hashtag APIs to use GORM model-based queries instead of raw Table(...) calls, while preserving existing response shapes.

Scope

Included APIs:

  • GET /search/hashtag
  • GET /search/hashtag-post

Skipped APIs:

  • GET /search/sl/hashtag
  • GET /search/sl/post-by-hashtag

Slim-only APIs are skipped for now because they are not the current app priority.

Requirements

1. Use GORM Models

Replace raw table/view targeting:

Config.DB.Table("views_hashtag")
Config.DB.Table("hashtag_by_user")
Config.DB.Table("views_timeline_post_slim")

with model-based queries:

Config.DB.Model(&Models.ViewsHashtag{})
Config.DB.Model(&Models.HashtagByUser{})
Config.DB.Model(&Models.ViewsTimelinePostSlim{})

2. Use Proper Model Containers

  • Avoid []map[string]interface{} for query result containers.
  • Avoid scanning view data into unrelated response DTOs when a matching table/view model exists.
  • Use view/table models for intermediate query results.
  • Keep response DTOs only where they define the API response contract.

3. Preserve Response Shape

  • Do not add fields to responses.
  • Do not remove existing response fields.
  • Do not expose internal fields like encrypt, category_id, or table-only identifiers unless the API already returned them.
  • Use json:"-" on internal model fields that are needed for filtering but should not be returned.

4. Hashtag Query Parameter

The tag parameter must be URL-encoded when it contains #.

Correct:

/search/hashtag-post?tag=%23happy

Incorrect:

/search/hashtag-post?tag=#happy

Unencoded # is treated as a URL fragment and is not sent to the server, causing tag to be empty.

Verification

Run:

go test ./...

Expected result: pass.

issues.display_title: Issue #477: Users Account GORM Model Query Migration
issues.main_description_html:
RESULT 03/08/26

✅ Implementation: Users GORM Model Query Migration

Overview

This document outlines the first Users module query migration from raw Table(...) usage to GORM Model(...) usage.

Updated API:

  • GET /users/account
  • File: src/Action/V1/Users/ListUserAccount.go

Files Modified

  1. src/Action/V1/Users/ListUserAccount.go

Implementation Details

1. Query Target Update

Replaced raw table targeting:

Config.DB.Table("user_account")

with GORM model targeting:

Config.DB.Model(&Models.UserAccount{})

Full query:

qUserAccount := Config.DB.Model(&Models.UserAccount{}).
    Select("facebook_id, facebook_email, facebook_fullname, google_id, google_email, apple_id, apple_email").
    Where("user_id = ?", userId).
    Scan(&userAccount)

2. Response Preservation

The API still scans into:

Models.UserAccountData

This preserves the existing account response and prevents table-only fields from being returned:

  • id
  • user_id
  • created_at
  • updated_at

3. No Manual Mapping Loop

The selected DB columns map directly to the response DTO, so no manual loop or extra conversion is needed.

Verification

Ran:

go test ./...

Result: pass.

Objective

Update non-slim Users APIs to use GORM model-based queries instead of raw Table(...) calls, while preserving existing API response shapes.

Scope

Initial API:

  • GET /users/account
  • File: src/Action/V1/Users/ListUserAccount.go

Slim-only APIs are skipped unless they are part of a hybrid flow needed by the current app.

Requirements

1. Use GORM Models

Replace raw table targeting:

Config.DB.Table("user_account")

with model-based query targeting:

Config.DB.Model(&Models.UserAccount{})

2. Preserve Response Shape

  • Keep scanning into Models.UserAccountData.
  • Do not return table-only fields such as id, user_id, created_at, or updated_at.
  • Do not rename JSON keys.
  • Do not change encryption or response wrapper behavior.

3. Avoid Manual Mapping

Use GORM Scan(...) directly into the existing response DTO when selected columns already match the response fields.

Preferred pattern:

var userAccount Models.UserAccountData

Config.DB.Model(&Models.UserAccount{}).
    Select("facebook_id, facebook_email, facebook_fullname, google_id, google_email, apple_id, apple_email").
    Where("user_id = ?", userId).
    Scan(&userAccount)

Verification

Run:

go test ./...

Expected result: pass.
